focus: OpenVerified handle and SQLite identity binding
summary: The catalog-HMAC inconsistency is closed by removing the undefined HMAC test; catalog corruption, quarantine, tombstones, CSRF, key, and threat-boundary controls are coherent. The SQLite contract remains internally inconsistent: it requires PRAGMA database_list before first SQL even though the PRAGMA is SQL, and SQLite is opened by path rather than consuming the verified handle in the VFS.

round12_dispositions.evidence: §6 negative cases now cover catalog ACL/owner, malformed format, file-ID, write, and Sync failures; the undefined catalog-HMAC assertion is removed.

findings.title: SQLite file identity verification is not pre-SQL as written
findings.evidence: §3 opens SQLite by canonical path in mode=rw and says a connection hook checks PRAGMA database_list and OS file ID before the first SQL. PRAGMA database_list is itself SQL, and a path-opened connection is not directly consuming the verified OpenVerified handle through VFS.
findings.risk: The required no-access-before-file-identity-check invariant is not precisely implementable as written; an implementation could execute SQL or read DB content before validating that the SQLite connection uses the authorized object.
findings.required_revision: Use the verified handle directly in the pilot VFS and expose its OS file ID before any database operation, or specify a VFS-level post-open/pre-SQL identity callback with a guarantee of no page/schema read or write before comparison. Do not use PRAGMA as a pre-SQL check; keep fail closed where the modernc API cannot provide the guarantee.

control_dispositions.catalog_hmac_mismatch: closed; undefined MAC negative case removed

remaining_conditions: Resolve PSK-SEC13-01 before implementing the SQLite open/identity boundary.
limitations: No tests or runtime validation were run.
No SQLite/VFS API, ACL, catalog, browser request, key, DB, or recovery path was inspected at runtime.
This review does not approve implementation, production deployment, real student data, or classroom readiness.
